messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D intake did not differ between elderly Japanese participants with and without depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "The consumption of all vitamins, except for retinol and vitamin D, was lower among depressed than non-depressed participants."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (short version of the Geriatric Depression Scale)
Population: 1634 elderly Japanese individuals aged 65 years and older
Intervention: Dietary vitamin D intake measured by brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire
Comparator: Participants without depressive symptoms
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,634
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Lower 25OHD levels were correlated with more severe depressive symptoms in first-episode psychosis patients.
Sentence: "Low 25OHD was significantly correlated with high severities of depressive (r=-0.484, p=0.004) and negative (r=-0.480, p=0.005) symptoms as well as general psychopathology (r=-0.569, p=0.001) in FEP patients."
Measured as: depression (Beck Depression Inventory)
Population: Adults aged 18-45 years with affective and non-affective first-episode psychosis presenting to an early intervention team in Portugal
Intervention: None (observational; serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level)
Comparator: Not applicable (correlation across participants)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 66
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A measures dietary vitamin D intake in older adults while Study B measures serum 25OHD in first-episode psychosis patients; both are cross-sectional, with different populations and exposure measures.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: elderly community Japanese (n = 1634) vs first-episode psychosis patients aged 18-45 (n = 66); exposure: dietary intake questionnaire vs serum 25OHD level"}
